title: How sounds link
subtitle: 연음
review: Written by Claude. The Korean and the romanization have not been checked by a Korean speaker. No audio yet: the Korean voice is not chosen.
intro: Korean is written in syllable blocks, but it is not said block by block. A final consonant slides over to the next syllable when that one starts with a vowel. This is why the romanization does not always match the Hangul letter for letter.

groups.title: The final consonant moves over
notes: A final consonant followed by a vowel is said at the start of the next syllable: 한국어 is written han-guk-eo and said han-gu-geo.

groups.title: Nose sounds spread
notes: Before m or n, a final k, t or p turns into ng, n or m. It is easier to say, and everyone does it.

groups.title: Longer words
notes: Listen for how each one differs from its spelling.
